content.comment_body: Hello, if I have several [product_name] devices, can each device use the maximum network inputs and outputs independently? For example, for device 1, what is the maximum number of network inputs—24? And for device 2, same question. I am trying to understand how the limits apply when using multiple modules. [user_name]
For each [product_name] with [article_no], you can use: 64 digital network inputs, 64 digital network outputs, 32 analog network inputs, and 16 analog network outputs.
If I have two [product_name] devices, does each one support 64 network inputs separately? Why does the demo version restrict it to 24 inputs?

It seems you did not mention that you are using a [product_name] with [article_no]. Your post was moved from a topic about the [article_no] variant. The [article_no] version can also handle 64 network inputs. However, if you want a [product_name] with [article_no] set as a slave to read digital hardware inputs, it is limited to 24 digital hardware inputs.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing the maximum network input/output limits for multiple [product_name] devices and expressing confusion over the distinction between software network input limits and hardware input capacities, especially when using different device versions or demo software. The conversation highlights typical misunderstandings regarding the differences between network and physical hardware limitations and their implementation in various [product_name] versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that each [product_name] can utilize the full set of network inputs and outputs, independent of other modules, and expect no reduction in capabilities due to hardware type or use of a demo version.
